There are also explicit company disclosures of neural-symbolic methods, including AlphaGeometry2. Neither general opacity nor individual disclosures settle whether secrecy greatly impoverished this field.
limitations: The main transparency audit concerns 2024 and the broader foundation-model ecosystem.

Undisclosed experiments are difficult to count from public records.

evidence.publisher: Bommasani et al., TMLR; arXiv version
evidence.explanation: The audit documents substantial opacity but also an improvement in average transparency from 37 to 58 out of 100. It concerns foundation-model transparency generally and does not measure lost neurosymbolic research or establish that secrecy caused such a loss.

The AlphaGeometry2 paper explicitly describes its neural-symbolic predecessor and details changes to the language model, symbolic engine, formal language, and search. This is material evidence of company disclosure, although one disclosed system cannot establish the overall disclosure rate or eliminate research losses elsewhere.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A documented inventory of withheld neurosymbolic methods, linked to substantial replication failures or delayed findings, ideally with evidence showing how disclosure changed public research outcomes.
